claims.claim: Andrej Karpathy used Claude Opus 5.5 to build a Civilization-style US map from 31 real government datasets in 7 hours and 45 minutes, producing 45K lines of code.
claims.episode_span: Andrej Karpathy asked Claude Opus 5.5 to populate a Civilization-style game map with real US public data. Opus downloaded and parsed 31 sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA and CDC, then reconciled elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows and disasters onto a single 25 km hex grid. The model mapped real metrics into game terms—GDP became gold yield, San Jose received a Campus district, Detroit became Motor City—and assigned citizen specializations based on actual workforce data such as one in four San Jose workers being engineers, coders or scientists. It added 19 lenses covering income, degrees, faith and disasters, a City View for 524 metros, nine advisors and an Explorer that converts any column across 3,100+ counties into tables and scatter plots linked to the map. The project ran for 7 hours and 45 minutes, produced 45K lines of code, and is now live for anyone to browse and extend.
claims.source_title: Claude builds detailed Civilization-style US map using real public data — Andrej Karpathy (2026-11-26)
claims.supporting_quote: I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

claims.claim: MGMem uses a deterministic discriminative-parser pipeline instead of generative LLM calls to build long-horizon agent memory, outperforming baselines on LoCoMo without generative indexing.
claims.episode_span: MGMem replaces the usual generative-LLM summarization step in long-horizon agent memory with a deterministic discriminative-parser pipeline that builds an incidence graph from recurring mentions across sessions. The system resolves question mentions through a subject-conditioned three-stage resolver and returns the original raw dialogue episodes instead of synthesized text, eliminating thousands of generative calls per build, non-determinism, and loss of provenance. On English multi-session dialogue QA it outperforms matched-protocol baselines on LoCoMo without any generative indexing and remains competitive on the full LongMemEval-S benchmark while leading or tying on single-session retrieval tasks.
claims.source_title: MGMem: An Efficient, Deterministic, and Provenance-Preserving Framework for Long-Horizon Agent Memory
claims.supporting_quote: We propose MGMem, a framework with no generative indexing calls that replaces this step with a deterministic discriminative-parser pipeline: recurring mentions across sessions are organized into an incidence graph, question mentions are resolved by a subject-conditioned three-stage resolver, and raw dialogue episodes are returned to the reader. On English multi-session dialogue QA, MGMem outperforms matched-protocol baselines on LoCoMo without generative indexing calls.

claims.claim: NVIDIA open-sourced Synthetic Charts V1 with 9.98M examples, Synthetic Tables V1 with 1M examples, and OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 with 7.9M examples for Nemotron 3.5 Parse training.
claims.episode_span: The team open-sourced three datasets: Synthetic Charts V1 with 9.98M examples, Synthetic Tables V1 with 1M examples, and OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 with 7.9M examples, all used to improve chart and table extraction through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.
claims.source_title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference — Hugging Face Blog
claims.supporting_quote: We are open-sourcing three datasets used in the Parse 3.5 training : Synthetic Charts V1 — 9.98M examples : rendered charts and structured annotations for learning categories, series, and numerical values. Synthetic Tables V1 — 1M examples : rendered HTML tables with targets that preserve rows, columns, headers, and cell relationships. OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 — 7.9M examples : synthetic document pages with Parse-format targets across varied fonts and layouts, for multilingual OCR and structured page reading.
